summary: This House rules resolution sets procedures for floor consideration of H.J. Res. 25 (disapproving an IRS digital-asset broker reporting rule), H.R. 1156 (extending the statute of limitations on unemployment fraud), and H.R. 1968 (further FY2025 continuing appropriations), waiving points of order, deeming specified amendments adopted, limiting debate to one hour, and allowing one motion to recommit for each measure.

scores.thoughts: The resolution enables floor consideration of H.R. 1968, a continuing appropriations measure that funds government operations at existing levels through extensions. This is procedural and does not itself expand or contract overall spending, so the bill has no meaningful directional effect on the topic.

Section 1 facilitates a joint resolution (H.J. Res. 25) disapproving an IRS broker-reporting rule for digital-asset gross proceeds. Disapproval prevents a new tax-information-reporting requirement; the connection is tangential and does not alter tax rates, so the effect is minor and leans toward reduced compliance burden.

Section 2 enables H.R. 1156, which lengthens the statute of limitations for prosecuting fraud in CARES Act unemployment programs. This strengthens enforcement against improper payments in a safety-net program and therefore leans modestly toward tightening rather than expanding benefits.
